hero.subheadline: Artists of every level enter up to twenty original artworks
hero.valueProposition: The overall winner receives a £2,000 cash prize, a solo exhibition at Panter & Hall's Cecil Court Gallery, a bundle of STAEDTLER materials, and a six-page feature.

content.whyJoin:
The British Art Prize, run by Artists & Illustrators magazine, is an annual art competition showcasing the talent and diversity of contemporary artists from around the world. Open to everyone - amateur, emerging, or professional - it considers all styles, media, and techniques, with the exception of works generated by AI. A panel of leading curators, gallerists, and art professionals selects up to 75 shortlisted artworks.

The shortlisted works are exhibited at London's OXO Gallery, giving thousands of visitors the chance to see and collect new art. The 2026 exhibition runs from 21-25 October, with a private view reception on 22 October for artists, collectors, and VIP guests. Shortlisted works are also showcased in an online gallery where they are available to purchase.

Winners receive prizes worth more than £10,000, including cash awards, art materials from STAEDTLER, Derwent, Royal Talens, and Clairefontaine, a solo exhibition at Panter & Hall's Cecil Court Gallery, and editorial features in Artists & Illustrators, the UK's best-selling art magazine.
content.whoShouldApply:
The British Art Prize is open to everyone - amateur, emerging, and professional artists from any country. All styles, media, and techniques are considered, and artists may submit up to 20 original works. The entry fee is £24 for the first artwork and £19 for each additional work, and submissions are made online with digital images of the artwork.

Works generated by AI are not accepted, and selected artists must be able to deliver the physical artwork for the exhibition at OXO Gallery from 21-25 October 2026. The competition connects selected artists with a combined audience of nearly one million art lovers and collectors.

This call suits artists who want a far-reaching platform for publicity and recognition, the chance to exhibit in a central London gallery, and an opportunity to sell work to a large audience of collectors.

faq.question: Who can enter the British Art Prize?
faq.answer: The prize is open to everyone - amateur, emerging, and professional artists from any country. All styles, media, and techniques are considered, with the exception of works generated by AI.

faq.question: How much does it cost to enter?
faq.answer: The entry fee is £24 for the first artwork and £19 for each additional artwork, up to 20 works per artist. Entries are submitted online with digital images of the artwork.

faq.question: What is the entry deadline?
faq.answer: Submissions close at 5pm on Friday, August 7, 2026. Artists enter by completing the online entry form and uploading digital images of their work.

faq.question: What are the prizes?
faq.answer: The overall winner receives £2,000 cash, a solo exhibition at Panter & Hall's Cecil Court Gallery, STAEDTLER art materials, and a six-page feature. The second prize is £500 cash with £750 of Derwent materials, and the third prize is £750 of Royal Talens products. A dedicated portraiture prize awards £750 cash.

faq.question: What happens after submission?
faq.answer: Judges select a shortlist of up to 75 artworks, including the five top prize winners. The shortlist and the People's Choice public vote go live online on September 25, 2026.

faq.question: Where is the exhibition held?
faq.answer: Shortlisted works are exhibited at London's OXO Gallery from 21-25 October 2026, with a private view reception on 22 October. Works are also shown in an online gallery where they can be purchased.

submissionGuide.detail: Submit digital images of your artwork through the competition entry page before the deadline. The entry fee is £24 for the first artwork and £19 for each additional work, with up to 20 works allowed.

A panel of curators, gallerists, and art professionals selects a shortlist of up to 75 artworks, including the five top prize winners. The shortlist and People's Choice vote go live online on September 25, 2026.
Shortlisted artists must make the physical artwork available for the exhibition stage, so it can be delivered to London ahead of the show.
The exhibition runs at OXO Gallery from 21-25 October 2026, with a private view reception on 22 October for artists, collectors, and VIP guests.
The winners are revealed at the private view, and prize-winning and shortlisted works are featured in the Artists & Illustrators winners' special issue.
